title: It works
text:
It works. Cambom Manual Mandoline Slicer does what it's suppose to do. My mandoline slicer needed replaced, so I choose this one to try. I have mixed feelings about it. I sliced onions and mushrooms with it, it did well for both, the blades are sharp. I do really like the spring in the holder, so it presses the veggies towards the blade. The bottom holds a good capacity and the plastic should not shatter easily. However, it feels very cheap. The top is two parts, not removable from each other but not waterproof. I hand washed this in my filled sink before use, and the top had some water trapped inside, I had to rinse and rinse to make sure all the soapy water was out. 6 blades are included, two are very useful, a couple I'll probably never use. The plastic one is a mystery to me it has holes, I have no idea what it's supposed to be for since it's just plastic holes with a little texture to it, the plastic is soft, so I can't see how this will really work. A case is included, but it only holds 3 blades. The other 3 must be stored in bottom side of the top, I don't like that. When I go to use it, I have to either remove 2 of the blades, and have no good place to set them, or leave them in place and have 3 blades to wash every time. I don't like handling these blades any more that when I use them. I wish the case cold hold 5 of the blades instead, that would be more useful to me. A veggie peeler is included, it's okay, but the handle isn't very sturdy. It will peel carrots okay, but I wouldn't trust is with thick-skinned potatoes. The brush is good, and does get into the nooks and crannies of the blades when it's time to clean.

Overall, I wouldn't strongly recommend this mandoline because it requires handling blades more than necessary and the top is not water-tight. I do find that for the quality, this is not a good value.
